newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA says welcomes financial services reform.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA says welcomes financial services reform.

text.p: Britain's financial watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Tuesday it welcomed the reforms proposed by British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown to financial services regulation.

"I share your aspiration that substantial gains may be made by reducing the complexity and overlap of the current system, while enhancing investor protection and reducing compliance costs," said SFA chairman Nicholas Durlacher in a letter to the UK Treasury.
"I particularly welcome the scope of your intended reforms to include more than just the SIB (Securities and Investments Board) and the SRO's (self-regulating organisations)," he said.
Brown said in a statement to parliament that reforms to simplify the financial services regulation would start immediately.
Britain's top financial regulator the SIB would become the only financial regulator, taking in the previously self-regulating organisations set up by the Financial Services act of 1986, Brown said.
